lines.name: l1
lines.text: You walk into the kitchen. And you have no idea why you came.

lines.name: l2
lines.text: It's not your memory failing. It's the door.

lines.name: l3
lines.text: In 2011, psychologist Gabriel Radvansky had people carry objects between rooms.

lines.name: l4
lines.text: Those who walked through a doorway forgot more than those who walked the same distance inside one room.

lines.name: l5
lines.text: His explanation: your brain treats a doorway as an event boundary. It closes one chapter and files it away.

lines.name: l6
lines.text: The fix? Walk back to the room where you had the thought. It often comes right back.
